leads.work: Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.
leads.why: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process.

leads.work: Customers send nomination and actuals spreadsheets by email (TXU's hplMMDD.xls and 'Enron Actuals'; Reliant/Copano egmnom and HPL-month xls; Devon avails). Ami Chokshi forwards them by hand to five or six schedulers.
leads.why: These come daily or several times a day as xls attachments, and each one is retyped or forwarded. A shared inbox, an EDI feed or automatic loading would remove the forwarding.

leads.work: Expired Sitara deals cause bridgeback errors, allocation exceptions and feedback errors. Each one starts an email chain asking Daren to extend the deal or create a new one, often to cover tiny spillover volumes (0.3 to 24 dec). Volume Management then sets up a manual accounting arrangement, or parks the gas on stranger's gas.
leads.why: This is the most common thread in the batch. Each case passes through 3 to 5 people (allocator → logistics → Daren → back), with deadlines tied to close. Aimee states that an accounting arrangement 'is always created every month' for meter 7266 and for the Cilco withdrawal, and Volume Management wants a deal so it doesn't have to make one every month. Possible fixes: evergreen or auto-roll rules, a tolerance for small overflow volumes, and an automatic expiry report before month end.

leads.work: UA4 (unaccounted-for gas) cleanup for 1997–1999 production months. Staff dig through OSS, CPR and MIPS to find missing deals or contracts for old meter volumes on the 089 contract.
leads.why: Many requests, each needing manual research across several legacy systems. Answers depend on staff who have left, and some issues sat open for months (the PanEnergy meter 4045 thread ran from May 1999 to Jan 2000). Desk-to-desk and park-and-ride bookings have no documented procedure.

leads.work: Kim Vaughn builds an HL&P flow spreadsheet (month-to-date and monthly) and emails it to Janet Wallis. Shortfall days are then handled by hand, with buyback or penalty decisions made under the contract's tolerance.
leads.why: The spreadsheet goes out weekly or more often ('most recent numbers'). The shortage and penalty calculation follows a fixed rule (5% tolerance, makeup days), so it could be computed automatically.

leads.work: Producer Services (Vance Taylor, Susan Smith, Donald Reinhardt, Melissa Graves) emails new well turn-ons and spot or baseload ticket details. Logistics (Tom Acton) keys them into Sitara and replies with the ticket number. Wellhead volume-change requests and monthly production estimates follow the same route.
leads.why: The same templated email (counterparty, meter, volume, price) is retyped into Sitara each time. A correction email (GMT price) shows the errors this invites. Tom asks for 'a lotus note with all the info' so he can file it. A form or direct entry would remove the handoff.

leads.work: KCS sends Josey Ranch monthly nomination estimates and intramonth revisions by email. Susan Trevino forwards them, and someone updates the volumes by hand.
leads.why: These recur every month, with revisions in between, and pass through forward-and-rekey steps.

leads.work: Monthly setup of industrial customers: buybacks, swings, ranking, deficiency deals, the Julie Meyers buyback spreadsheet, the industrial report, and force-majeure calls. This includes Valero's per-meter base, swing and buyback tickets with retroactive repathing and accounting arrangements.
leads.why: Every month there is a buyback list, a spreadsheet update, a report for Gas Control, and setup deadlines (3rd workday) that get missed. Rules for buyback versus force majeure are settled by email each time a plant goes down. Robert Lloyd's pathing procedure memo shows how complex the manual pathing is. The handover from Ken Seaman went badly and the report lapsed for months.

leads.work: Monthly cost-allocation and survey work for managers: RC allocation percentage spreadsheets (with protected cells that block corrections), activity 'Hours' surveys for each position, activity driver quantity surveys, checks of analyst charges, PC purchase reviews, and salary survey questionnaires.
leads.why: These recur every month with short deadlines. Brenda gave up on the spreadsheet because she couldn't insert a column. Shari Mao's survey email itself offers to take a standard report instead of the survey. The 'A and A Reclass' charges are a manual journal entry each month that managers must then check.

leads.work: Transport and service rates are missing or wrong in Sitara and Unify (expense reconciliation, PMAs, transport usage tickets that don't match Lauri's rate matrix), and pipeline invoices are reconciled against deal tickets by hand.
leads.why: Rates are fixed by hand during close each month. Two rate sources, the matrix and the tickets, get out of step and make the P&L estimate wrong.

leads.work: Intercompany (HPLC vs ENA) accrual and volume variances: one side of a deal is missing or volumes don't match, and settlements chases schedulers to fix it.
leads.why: Gregg Lenart lists $3.7M of mismatches in one month and states the goal of reducing analysis time. Thu Nguyen's chases show this recurs as month-end clearing.

leads.work: MOPS (Unify) and POPS nominations get out of sync, along with deal-ticket and nomination mismatches. Duplicate data entry in pathing includes Source and Destination rankings, deals ranked wrong, and repathing or renominating.
leads.why: The Shoreline case shows the systems disagreed for days without anyone noticing. Mark Schrab proposes defaulting destination rankings to cut time and errors. Dave Nommensen proposes purging the oversized Contract_Event_Status log.

leads.work: Volume discrepancy checks with pipelines and customers (PG&E at meter 8743, Oasis, Beaumont Methanol/Brandywine, Mid-Tex, Koch), done by comparing numbers day by day.
leads.why: Each one needs a manual day-by-day comparison and phone calls, with confusion over whom to contact.

leads.work: King Ranch, Three Rivers and HPLR Liquids scheduling: point noms, interconnect tickets, and identifying wellhead purchases.
leads.why: Errors persist (Pat: 'too many discrepancies... very costly to the desk'). The contracts were restructured, about 7,000/day stayed unidentified, and the work was redone repeatedly.

leads.work: Monthly nominations for the Enron Methanol and EGP MTBE plants, Sitara edits by the marketer, and requests to traders or risk to adjust risk assignment by hand.
leads.why: These come every month by email and need follow-up Sitara and risk changes (for example, wrong Gas Daily volumes).

leads.work: Recurring broadcast notices: the Unify close schedule, shut-in meter lists, counterparty DUNS and name-change lists, Sitara outage releases, and leap-day end-date fixes.
leads.why: The same templated mass emails go out monthly. Shut-in lists are forwarded again because recipients were left off. Leap-day deals needed a manual sweep.

leads.work: Out-of-office emails listing desk coverage, plus holiday on-call and contact lists.
leads.why: Frequent mass emails list who covers each pipeline or duty. A shared coverage matrix could replace them.

leads.work: Unclear desk assignments and handoffs leave gas unpathed (Hank Eisenhour's duties split), with staffing and scheduling-hours discussions.
leads.why: Several pipelines were left unassigned for weeks, and follow-up memos repeat the same open issues. A work-schedule committee discusses weekend coverage and cross-training.

leads.work: Cilco storage: a monthly withdrawal worksheet goes to the customer, plus complex manual pathing for storage injections and withdrawals.
leads.why: This is monthly and procedural. The pathing had to be worked out by Howard, who is outside Logistics, which raised concerns about who owns the role.

leads.work: Meter and pooling-point master-data setup: new pooling points, removing SCADA/MIPS and estimate-file entries for accounting meters, and Legal approval of new delivery-location text.
leads.why: These are repeated manual requests caused by wrong assumptions made when the meters were set up.

leads.work: Force-majeure letters and penalty billing for undertakes (Calpine, Valero), handled by finding the letters and faxing them.
leads.why: Settlement has to chase paper letters to support or reverse penalties.

leads.work: EOL deals are killed or modified after execution, and Product Control must be notified.
leads.why: The number of killed deals was rising, which costs audit trail and creates legal exposure. The proposed fix needs a manual termination agreement.
